title: GPG Commit Signing
description: Set up GPG commit signing to cryptographically verify your commits on GitHub and GitLab.

data.text: GPG (GNU Privacy Guard) commit signing adds a cryptographic signature to every commit. This proves that the commit was created by you and has not been tampered with. GitHub and GitLab display 'Verified' on signed commits and warn on unsigned or unverified commits.
Install GPG, generate a key pair, configure Git to use your key, and add the public key to GitHub or GitLab.

data.title: Generate and configure a GPG key
data.code:
# Install GPG
# Windows: choco install gnupg
# macOS: brew install gnupg
# Linux: apt-get install gnupg

# Generate a new GPG key
gpg --full-generate-key

# Select: (4) RSA (sign only)
# Key size: 4096
# Expiration: 1y (or no expiration)
# Name: Your Name
# Email: your-email@example.com
# Passphrase: (use a strong passphrase)

# List your keys
gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format=long

# Output shows:
# sec   rsa4096/ABCDEF1234567890 2024-01-01 [SC] [expires: 2025-01-01]
#      1234567890ABCDEF1234567890ABCDEF12345678
# uid                      Your Name <your-email@example.com>

# Copy the key ID: ABCDEF1234567890

data.text: Tell Git which GPG key to use and enable automatic signing for all commits.

data.title: Configure Git GPG signing
data.code:
# Configure Git to use your GPG key
git config --global user.signingkey ABCDEF1234567890

# Enable automatic signing for all commits
git config --global commit.gpgsign true

# Verify configuration
git config --global user.signingkey
git config --global commit.gpgsign

# Sign a single commit manually (without changing config)
git commit -S -m "chore: signed commit"

data.text: Export your GPG public key and add it to your GitHub account. GitHub then verifies commits signed with the corresponding private key.

data.title: Export and add GPG public key to GitHub
data.code:
# Export the GPG public key in ASCII format
gpg --armor --export ABCDEF1234567890

# Copy the output (between -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
# and -----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----)

# Add to GitHub:
# Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New GPG key → paste → Add GPG key

# After adding, GitHub shows 'Verified' on your signed commits

data.text: Use git log --show-signature to see verification status for each commit. A 'Good signature' line means the commit was signed and verified with a trusted key.

data.title: Verify commit signatures
data.code:
# Show signature status for recent commits
git log --show-signature -5

# Output for a verified commit:
# commit abc1234... (HEAD -> main)
# gpg: Signature made ... using RSA key ID ABCDEF12
# gpg: Good signature from "Your Name <your-email@example.com>"
# Author: Your Name <your-email@example.com>
# Date:   Mon Jan 01 12:00:00 2024 +0000
#     chore: signed commit

# Output for an unsigned commit:
# commit def5678...
# Author: Your Name <your-email@example.com>
# Date:   Mon Jan 01 12:00:00 2024 +0000
#     chore: unsigned commit

data.text: Tags are often signed to verify release integrity. Use git tag -s to create a signed tag. Verify with git tag -v.

data.title: Create and verify a signed tag
data.code:
# Create a signed tag
git tag -s v2.1.0 -m "Release version 2.1.0"

# Verify the tag signature
git tag -v v2.1.0

# Output:
# gpg: Signature made ... using RSA key ID ABCDEF12
# gpg: Good signature from "Your Name <your-email@example.com>"
# object abc1234...
# type commit
# tag v2.1.0
# tagger Your Name <your-email@example.com> ...
# Release version 2.1.0

items.question: Do I need a passphrase for my GPG key?
items.answer: Yes. A passphrase protects your private key if it is stolen. Use gpg-agent to cache your passphrase so you do not enter it for every commit.

items.question: Can I sign commits without a passphrase?
items.answer: Technically yes, but it defeats the purpose of signing. If your private key is compromised, an attacker can sign commits as you without a passphrase.

items.question: Why does GitHub show 'Unverified' on my commits?
items.answer: You have not added your GPG public key to your GitHub account, or the email on your GPG key does not match your GitHub account email.

items.question: Can I sign commits with multiple keys?
items.answer: Use git commit -S<key-id> to specify a key for a single commit. The configured default key is used when -S is passed without an argument.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Generate a GPG key pair with gpg --full-generate-key
Configure git config --global user.signingkey and commit.gpgsign
Export and add your GPG public key to GitHub
Use git log --show-signature to verify signed commits
Sign tags with git tag -s and verify with git tag -v
